content.text:
Currently, local development enables PostHog whenever both environment variables are set. Your frontend `.env` has both populated. The browser initializes PostHog without a development guard in [hooks.client.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/hooks.client.ts:9).

The `dev` flag only changes the log environment to `"development"` and makes missing configuration throw an error. It does **not** disable collection. Removing the variables currently causes an error during development.

The application sends:

- Search submissions, result selections, and member/funder tab selections through `posthog.capture()`. See [SearchPage.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/SearchPage.svelte:173) and [MemberIdentity.svelte](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/MemberIdentity.svelte:99).
- Search activity and retry logs through [posthog-logger.ts](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/lib/posthog-logger.ts:5).
- Unhandled errors and promise rejections through the SDK configuration, plus Svelte client errors through [handleError](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/frontend/src/hooks.client.ts:45). Console-error capture is disabled.

The smallest change would be an early `if (dev) return` in `init()`, before configuration checks, plus a development guard in `handleError()`. That prevents SDK initialization and explicit exception reporting during development.

This is verified from source and configuration presence. I haven't checked live browser network traffic or changed anything.
